To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the beginning principals who participated in the Louisiana LEAD program were able to access and value information, but were unable to utilize it effectively.

(1) Beginning principals in LEAD schools use more external sources of information, (2) they value the external information more, (3) they are more likely than experienced principals to value external information as a source of decision-making information, and (4) the more experienced principals value internal information more than external information as a resource for making decisions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how information is used In schools that have adopted some form of shared decision making.
how principals access, use and value information in restructuring schools.
understanding the role of the information utilized by beginning principals in the process of restructuring schools.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a positive relationship between the extent to which teachers perceive themselves as involved in the decision making process and the valuing and use of information by the principal.
beginning principals are more likely than experienced principals to value information, and that they are also more likely than experienced principal to use information from external sources.
the more a school is restructured to involve teachers in shared decision making, the more likely it is that principals will be able to utilize information to make informed decisions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found that principals in the LEAD schools were using a wide variety of information to make decisions and that they valued this information, especially when it came from the teachers.
the principal is a central player in the restructuring process, and the role of the principal is critical in the implementation of school reform.
information utilization and decision-making are important to the success of school reform and restructuring.

we have to make a distinction between the way people think and the way they act.
beginning principals are in a unique position to use information in a way that is likely to be beneficial to their schools.
